div.p: At the 2024 Latin American and Caribbean Digital Humanities Symposium at the Universidad de San Francisco in Quito, Ecuador, Juan Pablo Viteri delivered a keynote talk on the multimedia project Radio COCOA . During his presentation, he made a statement that ran counter to what a DH audience might expect: “lo que menos me interesa de las humanidades digitales es la parte digital” (what interests me least about the digital humanities is the digital part). Rather than taking a stance against technology, however, Viteri was pointing to the fact that scholarly work built around the use of digital methods and tools allows us to do things that are not inherently digital: innovate, collaborate, and build communities. As the example of Radio COCOA makes clear, utilizing technology allowed Viteri and his team to rethink the scholarship they create, their methods for achieving those products, and the audiences they seek to reach.

This special issue proposes that the use of digital tools to achieve objectives that are not fundamentally digital is a central and defining activity in the context of Latin American and Latinx digital humanities. In many cases, those outcomes relate to highlighting and correcting injustice, promoting solidarity, and altering the ways we teach about Latin America and Latinx populations in the U.S. We do not argue that all digital work related to Latin America and Latinx communities should be understood as “public digital humanities” or “digital public humanities.” Instead, we suggest that the commitment to advocacy and social justice that informs scholarship in these areas frequently leads to the use of digital tools to achieve goals that focus not on technology but on building connections beyond academic spaces and engaging with real problems faced by actual people.

The projects examined in this special issue represent a small selection of the work taking place within Latin American and Latinx digital humanities that reflects such a vision. The program of the 2025 Latin American and Caribbean Digital Humanities Symposium, a six-day event held in Puerto Rico and online, demonstrates this point. Responding to the conference theme of Digital Humanities, Memory and Community, nearly 200 researchers, archivists, community members, students, and others came together to discuss numerous projects that are concerned with using digital methods to carry out collective action, preserve community memory, and build solidarity with communities .

For over a decade, experts have been warning of the dire state of the humanities in the U.S. academy ;;. An emphasis on STEM fields beginning in the early 2010s led many to question the value of the humanities, an attitude reinforced by political leaders who have openly denounced humanities fields as impractical and politically suspect. The increasing cost of higher education and uncertain economic conditions have led students wary of debt and fearing limited future opportunities to choose majors that lead to specific professional fields. In some states, performance funding metrics encourage institutional policies at public universities that disadvantage humanities fields, and recent attacks on diversity, equity and inclusion in higher education have placed restrictions on humanities curriculum and faculty speech. Declining enrollments in humanities majors provide a justification for defunding and eliminating critical programs in languages, literatures, and the arts, in particular.

The recent decline in the humanities in the U.S. academy is part of a long trend. As Eric Adler notes, the present circumstances reflect the continuation of a pattern of privileging practical education that dates from the late nineteenth century: As proponents of the humanities have noted for over a century, the humanistic disciplines were likely to wither in a system deliberately created to marginalize them . We may have reached a critical point in that process today, however, with some suggesting that the humanities may disappear from higher education altogether. On a recent episode of the New York Times podcast Hard Fork, for instance, historian D. Graham Burnett proposed that such an outcome is possible because the shifting economics of education have led administrators, parents and students to all focus on the return on [...] tuition investment and an increasingly exigent job market. Burnett suggests that the humanities must find other contexts in which to survive: the most important forms of that work are going to need to happen outside of colleges and universities .

As rapid social and technological transformation have created new challenges in recent years, the humanities have often not helped themselves by seeming resistant to change. Many scholars engage with today’s world but often do so using traditional methods and creating familiar types of products, usually books and scholarly articles, often working in isolation. To some extent, this is inevitable, as institutional structures and disciplinary expectations reward the production of traditional scholarly outputs while disincentivizing experimentation. The situation is exacerbated by the scarcity of tenure-track positions and the resulting exclusion of talented young scholars who could provide vision needed to transform our fields.

Teaching in the humanities, in particular, can often feel out of step with realities beyond the academy. We frequently adhere to traditional methods that ignore students' concerns over economic insecurity, do not effectively respond to a societal climate of anti-intellectualism, and fail to put pressure on entrenched institutional approaches. Our classrooms remain essential spaces for learning to think critically, communicate effectively, work collaboratively, and appreciate differences, but our students often lack access to the applied learning that might help them connect with communities, imagine their future professional selves and prepare for their lives after graduation.

As enrollments in humanities programs continue to decline, the advent of widely available artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT have added another layer of complexity to what already feels like a grim situation. Big Tech's pursuit of developing human-like intelligence feels dystopian and is, as authors signal, a scientific enterprise embedded in eugenicist ideologies. As such, some researchers assert that the humanities, as fields that deal with the complexities of being human, are more relevant than ever.

Laurent Dubreuil, for instance, argues in the recent book Humanities in the Time of AI that artificial intelligence offers a chance for the humanities to strengthen their relevance and their signification . Lauren Klein et al. make a similar point, observing that research related to AI has opened up new possibilities for conversation and collaboration between computing, engineering, and the humanities . Dubreuil and Klein et. al. advocate not only for more equitable interdisciplinary partnerships in our research and teaching, but for academic spaces in which humanities scholarship is viewed as central to addressing the many challenges facing human societies today.

Those whose professional activity revolves around the teaching of language and cultures, in particular, may reasonably question such optimism, however. The Modern Language Association reported a 29.3% drop in language enrollments between 2009 and 2021 (), prior to the release of ChatGPT in November 2022 and the recent surge in AI-related technologies that power simultaneous translation. In an Atlantic article titled The End of Foreign-Language Education, journalist Louise Matsakis reflected on watching a video of herself talking in perfect Chinese that she had generated using AI . Apple instructs users to [b]ridge language barriers in person — while traveling or navigating in a foreign country — with AirPods . A growing perception that language study is increasingly unnecessary in this context, combined with the emphasis on cost cutting and efficiency that is driving decisions at institutions, offers a grim outlook for language programs across the U.S. . Following the cancellation of all language programs at West Virginia University in 2023, news of the consolidation and closure of language programs, including at leading research institutions, has become common.

We also find ourselves in a time when the embrace of other cultures at the heart of much humanities scholarship is under attack. In recent years, resentments and fears that were once latent have transformed into unabashed and often violent vilification and dehumanization of those who are different and often the most vulnerable among us. Anti-immigrant sentiment and overt racism in the US have surged to levels not seen in decades, a reality that has grown more intense since January of 2025, as the second Trump administration has made anti-immigration action and legislation top priorities.

Latin Americans and Latinx populations in the US are among the groups particularly impacted by this open hostility. Masked ICE agents have abducted Latinx people from their homes and communities and incarcerated them without due process in improvised detention centers in the US, such as Florida’s “Alligator Alcatraz,” and in facilities abroad, including CECOT (Centro de Confinamiento del Terrorismo/Terrorism Confinement Center), a mega-prison in El Salvador ;;.
See also the digital project Torn Apart/Separados.
The Trump administration has withdrawn Temporary Protected Status for Haitians and Venezuelans living in the U.S. , . Many immigrants have expressed reluctance to leave their homes out of fear of detention, concerns validated by the Supreme Court’s recent approval of enforcement measures that rely on racial profiling ;;.

Students of Latin American origin face challenges not only in broader society but also in the particular context of higher education. They belong to communities that have historically encountered barriers to entering the system and have struggled to complete degrees, given the financial burdens and family responsibilities that they often must balance with their schoolwork ;;. The dismantling of affirmative action, the defunding of campus initiatives and programs aimed at promoting diversity and inclusion, and the federal government’s recent discontinuation of grants to Hispanic-Serving Institutions () make matters worse for these students, who often cannot see themselves reflected among faculty and their fellow students and fail to find a sense of belonging.

At the same time, the struggles of marginalized groups in Latin America itself continue unabated. In many places, violence against women and LGBTQIA+ individuals has become a normalized backdrop to everyday life. Indigenous communities face discrimination, the destruction of their lands, and sustained efforts to erase them from society. Those of African descent throughout the region must still fight for visibility, justice, and equal participation in societies that have long minimized their contributions or denied their existence. Community leaders and activists who resist injustice are routinely punished and assassinated ;.

In the face of all these realities, the need for new approaches to scholarship in the humanities is more urgent than ever. Scholars must project their activity into public spaces and engage with those outside the academy. They must demonstrate the value of their work. They likewise must provide students with opportunities to gain formative experiences beyond the classroom and help students of Latin American backgrounds find ways to create spaces of their own within higher education and beyond. Those whose work deals with marginalized peoples must build solidarity with those communities and co-create best practices for working together.

The projects described in this special issue, in particular, draw on community knowledge as a first step in countering or resisting fascism and white supremacy, both within and outside of academic institutions. To return to the first lines of this introduction, it is not the digital tools or methods that make these projects powerful, but rather the human relationships that are constructed and sustained across disciplines and among community stakeholders whose voices have historically been marginalized, sometimes even in the telling of their own histories. Here, we can consider Haiti, a Black nation in Latin America that, in addition to bearing the immediate burden of climate catastrophe caused by corporate actions in the Global North, continues to face racist typification and violence in North American and global media. The history of Haiti, as performer-scholar-activist reminds us, is deserving of “new narratives” — ones that are for and by Haitians. The articles in this special issue illuminate the significance of human relationships and community accountability within broader projects of countering hegemonic, racist, and fascist logics that continue to prescribe who gets to be human in the digital age.

head.hi: Approaches to Latin American and Latinx DH in the U.S., and Wider Implications

div.p: This special issue features articles about a collection of digital projects focused on Latin America and Latinx populations that speak to the notion of a more engaged, socially committed humanities. All are dedicated to connecting with communities, effecting change in the real world, and exploring collaborative modes of knowledge creation. They are all built on sophisticated theoretical foundations but carry out their work in accessible spaces in which non-academic publics are invested. Focusing on the meaningful human interaction at the center of the humanities, each of the projects suggests ways that our research and teaching can create shared experiences in which real people cannot be supplanted by technology. They demonstrate ways we can learn ways to intervene in society’s use of technology and shape it through humanistic inquiry.

Each project possesses a value that extends beyond its own particular worth, representing a model for a type of scholarship that others can emulate or adapt. Involving approaches that include digital oral history, the use of social media as tools for scholarly communication and community building, and the recovery and transmission of cultural heritage materials, they demonstrate ways that specific methodologies can be deployed to carry out scholarship that is participatory and dynamic. These projects point to innovative methods for incorporating digital methods into undergraduate classrooms, and exemplify approaches to reimagining the role of the scholar and teacher beyond the campus in the public sphere.

The authors of each article analyze critically how their work intersects with the notions of community, activism, and innovation. In doing so, they discuss their experiences conducting public-facing scholarship, explain the collaborative models they have developed, and consider the role of this work in their teaching and service. They examine the ethical aspects of their projects and their responsibilities as scholars, and in some cases as members of specific communities, working beyond traditional academic spaces. They analyze matters of positionality, considering how they locate themselves in relation to the communities they study or with whom they collaborate.

While this special issue focuses specifically on DH practice within the study of Latin America and Latinx communities in the U.S., the collection intersects with broader concerns within the digital humanities globally. The articles all address the mission, as expressed by DHQ itself, to achieve social change and social justice, and to make the field of digital humanities visible as a space for racial and gender equity . They do so by providing a forum for scholars of color to discuss, on their own terms, the challenges of conducting scholarly work of importance to their communities. Most of the contributors to this special issue identify as non-white and work in academic and cultural traditions that are underrepresented in DH scholarship and institutional spaces.

Similarly, as the majority of the contributors to this special issue are women, we believe this project highlights the leadership that women scholars are playing in the development of transformational work within public DH. Not only do their efforts often center the experience of gender and intersectionality, but they also demonstrate the potential of digital methods for illuminating and countering the logics of patriarchy and white supremacy as they operate within higher education and research spaces. Their work focuses on building communities and redefining scholarly objectives in the contexts of teaching, research and service, and their diverse scholarly approaches suggest ways to challenge patriarchal and racist paradigms by emphasizing methodologies that emphasize empathy, self-awareness, respect for difference, non-hierarchical structures, ethical practices and attention to intersectionality.

This special issue embraces another kind of diversity by centering the voices of junior scholars. Three of the four guest editors and most of the authors are early-career scholars. In this way, the collection showcases the commitment of the DH community to creating space for the ideas of the young scholars who, despite the difficult professional circumstances they often face in today’s academy, are working creatively and tirelessly to define the future of the field.

We believe this special issue contributes to promoting the international, multilingual character of the digital humanities. The collection points to a DH geography that expands beyond the boundaries of the Anglophone world and Western Europe, reaching into cultural spaces across Latin America and the Caribbean and exploring the often invisible transnational, transborder, and diasporic geographies within the United States of communities that have their roots in those regions. The editors and authors likewise seek to engage with questions about what it means to do DH in languages other than English, and, following the initial release of this special issue, will subsequently publish each article in at least one other language: Spanish, French, or Haitian Creole. An addendum to this introduction will be published once all the translations are added.

This special issue also asks questions about how we define DH, responding to DHQ’s standing call for contributions that “probe the boundaries of the domain or re-examine its foundational premises.” The articles in this special collection demonstrate a type of DH that does not privilege the digital nor the traditional humanities, but rather uses digital tools and humanities frameworks to engage with real communities and the challenges they face. DH itself has been considered a kind of “applied humanities,” but these projects go a step further, working in service of goals that make a real and immediate difference to people who have been neglected not only by society but also the academy. In doing so, this special issue seeks to speak to an active, committed DH that is both political and profoundly personal.

In addressing these topics, this collection fits into a series represented by several recent special issues of DHQ. Through its focus on diversity and inclusion, this issue connects with Black Digital Humanities in the Rising Generation (, Minimal Computing (16.2, 2022), Digital Sankofa: Understanding the Past and Futures of Black Digital Humanities (18.4, 2024), and most recently, The Politics and Ethics of Naming the Names of Enslaved People in Digital Humanities Projects (19.1, 2025). By highlighting non-Anglophone traditions, this issue also relates to the special issues on DH in Spanish (12.1, 2018) and Portuguese (14.2, 2020), and the collection Digital Humanities & Colonial Latin American Studies (14.4, 2020). Through their attention to the pedagogical implications of their work, the authors also address topics that relate to Imagining the DH Undergraduate: Special Issue in Undergraduate Education in DH (11.3, 2017).

Sylvia Fernández Quintanilla, Maira E. Álvarez, Carolina E. Alonso, and Laura Gonzales discuss United Fronteras, a collective of activists and scholars who critically examine the Mexico-US border as a fluid space endowed with multiple layers of meaning represented publicly and digitally through different forms and mediums. The group, consisting mostly women of color who have experienced the border region in different ways, co-created a registry of digital materials and projects that address questions of concern to the communities on both sides of that largely arbitrary and imaginary frontier, from before colonial times to the present. In their article, they consider the project’s use of minimal computing and its engagement with matters of cultural history, and political and gender violence, in order to reveal the complexities of a human space so often portrayed in simplistic and negative terms.

Siobhan Meï and Jonathan Michael Square reflect on their experience cofounding and leading Rendering Revolution: Sartorial Approaches to Haitian History. The project defines itself as a queer, bilingual, feminist experiment in digital interdisciplinary scholarship that uses the lens of fashion and material culture to trace the aesthetic, social, and political reverberations of the Haitian Revolution as a world-historical moment. Meï and Square examine the collaborative efforts of a team whose expertise lies in translation, visual culture, and cultural theory, and the project’s use of Instagram as a platform for analyzing Haitian history and culture. Presented as a conversation between the two authors, their contribution demonstrates how Rendering Revolution connects the past and present in ways that are visually compelling and argues for the power of social media as a tool for scholarly communication.

Constanza López Baquero analyzes Voces y Caras: Latinx Communities of North Florida, an oral history project in which Latinx students design and carry out interviews with local Hispanic residents at the University of North Florida Over the past thirteen years, hundreds of students and community members have participated, building a vast archive of stories focused on the realities of immigration, the experiences of women in Hispanic cultures, and the diversity found among those of Latin American origin in the US. In her article, López Baquero tells the story of the project, highlights a selection of interviews, and explains how, the project — through both its digital and non-digital components — showcases the perspectives of communities who are otherwise largely invisible in the region.

Nicole Willson considers Fanm Rebèl: Excavating the Histories of Haiti’s Women Revolutionaries, a three-year research project sponsored by the Leverhulme Trust and the Institute for Black Atlantic Research at the University of Central Lancashire. Fanm Rebèl seeks to excavate stories of women in the Haitian Revolution, highlighting radical acts of female insurgency and marronage and exploring narratives of resistance articulated through spiritual practice, domestic labor, creativity, survival, subterfuge and armed combat. In her article, Willson considers the project as a hub for collaboration between scholars, collectors, conservators, archivists and other interested parties in the community.

Lauren Royes-Baccus reflects on Salt & Aloes as a digital platform for radical systems of knowledge sharing through which Caribbean material and visual culture can be reimagined, reoriented, and resourced. The project seeks to unmoor the region from an aesthetic and projected conceptualization rooted in the abstracted and passive other. Royes-Baccus considers how the work of Salt & Aloes centers the Caribbean’s active use and transformation of objects, the generative praxis of creatives from/in/of the region, and the material restitution of its past, present and future.

Sylvia Mendoza Aviña considers MAS Muxeres: Oral Histories of Chicana/x leaders in Mexican American Studies Programs in San Antonio, Texas, as an oral history and digital humanities project that documents the contributions of the women laboring to keep the field alive and thriving. Despite their daily efforts to support MAS/Chicanx studies in their roles as program coordinators, instructors/professors, community organizers, and scholar activists, much of the institutional memory, organizing, and strategizing of these muxeres remains unrecorded. Mendoza Aviña argues that their knowledge is useful and necessary for current and future generations invested in not only sustaining, but building MAS/Chicanx studies, especially within places like Texas that are attempting to further whitewash school curriculum and texts through bills that attack critical race theory, diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI), and academic freedom.

Robert Irwin explores Humanizing Deportation, a participatory audiovisual project that since early 2017 has documented and disseminated the repercussions of contemporary migration and border control laws and policies on vulnerable migrants in the United States and Mexico. Through on-the-ground collaborations with deported migrants and asylum seekers in Tijuana and elsewhere, the project has published over 450 digital stories on its bilingual website. Irwin considers how Humanizing Deportation has increasingly developed strategies for incorporating undergraduate students into its research team, allowing these students, many of whose families are affected by such laws and policies, to become directly and meaningfully involved in helping migrants communicate their experiences and concerns to the world.

Eduard Arriaga-Arango studies Baobaixa, an initiative developed by the Afro-Brazilian network Rede Mocambos that serves as a model of community digital organizing as a way to propose data justice, digital sovereignty and autonomy. Baobaixa is a technology that interconnects diverse communities in Brazil (i.e, Quilombos, Indigenous communities and Favelas, among others), and also creates a structure to store, curate and disseminate local knowledge, traditions, histories and representations. In his article, Arriaga-Arango proposes Baobaixa as a model for how non-expert communities can use digital strategies to defend their territory, preserve their cultural production, and affirm their human condition.

This special issue showcases a collection of efforts, reflected in digital projects (in-process or finalized) in which technology is critical not on its own terms, but rather for the ways it allows scholars to engage in activities that are essentially non-digital in nature. By arguing that the use of technology can be instrumental — but is not the point — we believe the articles gathered here contribute to highlighting a paradox in the way DH has long been perceived by those outside the field. The “STEM for the humanities” paradigm has attracted administrators and provoked the suspicion of traditional humanities scholars, emphasizing the incorporation of digital tools into humanities scholarship as being, in some way, about technology. The articles gathered here demonstrate ways that much work in the digital humanities today is not fundamentally about technology, but rather about topics that, in some political and institutional contexts, may make decision makers uncomfortable and which our colleagues outside of DH might recognize as representing continuity with the work of the traditional humanities.

Much of DH remains highly computational in nature and much work arguably emerges from questions that are informed more by computer science than the traditional humanities. The expansion of the field in recent years, however, has brought a greater recognition that DH often involves using digital tools to counter injustice and construct communities, effecting work that points to new ways that the humanities can engage with the public and demonstrate their relevance in a world where the human experience is increasingly devalued. Like many of the projects highlighted here, such efforts often involve students and frequently imply a reconsideration of our collaborations as well as a reevaluation of what we teach, how, and why.

By bringing together the concepts of community and activism — both central to Latin American and Latinx scholarship — with an emphasis on the notions of intervention, innovation, and invention that characterize DH, this multilingual collection points to ways that the larger community of humanists and digital humanists can learn from the work being done by and with diverse populations that have survived historical injustices and continue to suffer and resist marginalization today, both within the US and throughout Latin America and the Caribbean. Highlighting, in particular, the work of interdisciplinary scholars of color, women scholars, and early-career scholars, this special issue offers models for designing hands-on, engaged humanities praxis that can better connect with and serve multilingual and multicultural students and diverse communities beyond the academy and across geographies.

Nan Senpozyòm 2024 Amerik Latin ak Syans Imanitè Nimerik Karayib la nan Inivèsite San Francisco nan Quito, Ekwatè, Juan Pablo Viteri te fè yon gwo diskou sou pwojè miltimedya Radyo COCOA . Pandan prezantasyon li a, li te fè yon deklarasyon ki te kontrè ak sa yon odyans DH (Digital Humanities) ta ka atann: lo que menos me interesa de las humanidades digitales es la parte digital (sa ki enterese m mwens sou syans imanitè nimerik yo se pati nimerik la). Olye pou l pran yon pozisyon kont teknoloji, Viteri t ap lonje dwèt sou lefèt ke travay akademik ki bati atravè itilizasyon metòd ak zouti nimerik yo pèmèt nou fè bagay ki pa natirèlman nimerik: inovasyon, kolabore, ak bati kominote yo. Tankou egzanp Radyo COCOA a fè li klè, itilize teknoloji pèmèt Viteri ak ekip li repanse bousdetid, rechèch yo kreye, metòd yo pou reyalize pwodwi sa yo, ak odyans y ap chèche rive sou yo.

Edisyon espesyal sa a pwopoze ke itilizasyon zouti nimerik pou reyalize objektif ki pa nimerik nan baz yo, se yon aktivite santral e prensipal nan kontèks syans imanitè nimerik nan Amerik Latin ak Latino. Nan plizyè ka, rezilta sa yo gen rapò ak mete aksan sou korije enjistis, ankouraje solidarite, ak chanje fason nou anseye popilasyon Amerik Latin ak Latino Ozetazini. Nou pa kont tout travay nimerik ki gen rapò avèk Amerik Latin ak kominote Latino yo ke yo ta dwe pèsevwa yo tankou "syans imanitè nimerik piblik" oswa "nimerik piblik syans imanitè." Okontrè, nou sijere ke angajman anvè defans ak jistis sosyal ki enfòme rechèch nan domèn sa yo, souvan mennen nan itilizasyon zouti nimerik pou atenn objektif ki pa konsantre sou teknoloji men sou bati koneksyon pi lwen pase espas akademik yo epi angaje yo ak pwoblèm reyèl moun reyèl yo ap fè fas.

Pwojè yo egzamine nan edisyon espesyal sa a reprezante yon ti seleksyon nan travay k ap fèt nan domèn syans imanitè nimerik nan kominote Amerik Latin ak Latino yo ki reflete vizyon sa a. Pwogram Senpozyòm 2025 Amerik Latin ak Syans Imanitè Nimerik nan Karayib la, se yon evènman sis jou ki te fèt nan Pòtoriko ak sou entènèt, li montre pwen sa a. Pou reponn a tèm konferans lan nan "Syans Imanitè Nimerik, Memwa ak Kominote," prèske 200 chèchè, achivis, manm kominote a, etidyan, ak lòt moun te rasanble pou diskite sou anpil pwojè ki konsène sou itilizasyon metòd nimerik pou fè aksyon kolektif, prezève memwa kominote a, ak bati solidarite avèk kominote yo .

Pou plis pase yon dizèn lane, ekspè yo t ap avèti sou sitiyasyon difisil syans imanitè yo nan akademi Ozetazini ;;. Yo mete aksan sou domèn STEM (syans teknoloji jeni matematik) ki nan kòmansman ane 2010 yo te mennen anpil moun kesyone valè syans imanitè yo, yon atitid ke lidè politik yo ranfòse, yo denonse piblikman syans imanitè yo tankou yon domèn ki pa pratik e ki politikman sispèk. Pri edikasyon siperyè ap monte e kondisyon ekonomik yo ensèten, sa rann etidyan yo pridan nan fè dèt epi yo pè; sa vin limite opòtinite nan avni yo pou chwazi filyè ki mennen nan yon domèn pwofesyonèl espesifik. Nan kèk eta, metrik finansman pèfòmans yo ankouraje politik enstitisyonèl nan inivèsite piblik yo ki pa nan avantaj domèn syans imanitè yo, e atak resan sou divèsite, ekite ak enklizyon nan edikasyon siperyè mete restriksyon sou kourikoulòm syans imanitè ak diskou fakilte yo. Yon rediksyon nan enskripsyon pou filyè syans imanitè yo bay yon jistifikasyon pou definanse ak elimine pwogram kritik nan lang yo, literati yo, ak atizay yo, an patikilye.

Dènyèman bès ki fèt nan syans imanitè nan akademi Ozetazini an fè pati de yon tandans ki dire lontan. Jan Eric Adler remake sa, sikonstans aktyèl yo reflete kontinyasyon yon modèl ki privilejye edikasyon pratik ki la depi nan fen diznevyèm syèk la: "Jan defansè syans imanitè yo te note pou plis pase yon syèk, disiplin imanis yo te gen anpil chans diminye nan yon sistèm ki te kreye tout ekspre pou majinalize yo" . Sepandan, jodi a, nou ka rive nan yon pwen kritik nan pwosesis sa a, gen kèk moun ki fè konnen ke syans imanitè yo ka disparèt nèt nan edikasyon siperyè. Nan yon epizòd resan sou podcast New York Times Hard Fork, pa egzanp, istoryen D. Graham Burnett te pwopoze ke yon rezilta konsa posib akoz de "chanjman nan ekonomi edikasyon an" sa te fè administratè, paran ak etidyan yo tout konsantre sou "retou sou [...] envestisman lajan yo peye lekòl la" ak yon mache travay ki de pli zan pli egzijan." Burnett sijere ke syans imanitè yo dwe jwenn lòt kontèks pou yo siviv: "fòm ki pi enpòtan nan travay sa yo pral bezwen fèt andeyò fakilte ak inivèsite yo .

Menm jan transfòmasyon rapid sosyal ak teknolojik te kreye nouvo defi nan dènye ane yo, syans imanitè yo pa souvan ede tèt yo lè yo bay ilizyon ke yo reziste a chanjman. Anpil entelektyèl enplike yo ak mond kounya men yo souvan fè sa pandan y ap sèvi avèk metòd tradisyonèl epi sa kreye kalite pwodwi familye yo tankou liv ak atik inivèsitè, anpil fwa y ap travay poukont yo. Nan yon sèten mezi, sa inevitab, paske estrikti enstitisyonèl ak atant disiplinè yo rekonpanse pwodiksyon rezilta inivèsitè tradisyonèl yo pandan y ap dekouraje eksperimantasyon. Sitiyasyon an vin pi mal paske gen yon ratman pozisyon pou pwofesè inivèsite ak esklizyon jèn entelektyèl ki gen talan ki te ka bay vizyon ki nesesè pou transfòme domèn nou yo.

Ansèyman nan syans imanitè yo, an patikilye, anpil fwa ka santi yo an dekalaj ak reyalite ki pi lwen pase akademi an. Nou respekte metòd tradisyonèl ki inyore enkyetid etidyan yo konsènan ensekirite ekonomik, ki pa reponn efektivman a yon klima sosyete anti-entelektyèl, epi ki pa mete presyon sou apwòch enstitisyonèl yo ki anrasinen. Sal klas nou yo rete espas esansyèl pou aprann panse kritik, kominike efektivman, travay ansanm, ak apresye diferans yo, men etidyan nou yo souvan pa gen aksè a aprantisaj aplike ki ta ka ede yo konekte ak kominote yo, imajine tèt yo nan lavni pwofesyonèl yo epi prepare yo pou lavi yo apre yo fin gradye.

Pandan enskripsyon nan pwogram syans imanitè yo kontinye ap bese, arive zouti entèlijans atifisyèl yo disponib toupatou tankou ChatGPT te ajoute yon lòt kouch konpleksite nan sa ki deja parèt tankou yon sitiyasyon makab. Pouswit Big Tech pou devlope entèlijans ki sanble ak sa moun ap fè sanble distopik (mizerab) epi, jan otè Timnit Gebru ak Émile P. Torres (2024) yo remake, yon antrepriz syantifik entegre nan ideyoloji ejenis yo. Se pou sa, gen kèk chèchè ki fè reklamasyon ke syans imanitè yo, kòm domèn ki fè fas avèk konpleksite kondisyon imen, yo vin pi enpòtan.

Pa egzanp, Laurent Dubreuil deklare nan denye liv li a Humanities in the Time of AI ke entèlijans atifisyèl "ofri yon chans pou syans imanitè yo ranfòse enpòtans ak siyifikasyon yo" (2025, 1). Lauren Klein et al. fè yon pwen menm jan an, li obsève ke rechèch ki gen rapò ak EA (Entelijans Atifisyèl) te "louvri nouvo posiblite pou konvèsasyon ak kolaborasyon ant enfòmatik, jeni, ak syans imanitè yo" (2025, 14). Dubreuil ak Klein et. al. defann non sèlman pou patenarya entèdisiplinè ki pi ekitab nan rechèch ak ansèyman nou yo, men pou espas akademik kote yo konsidere rechèch syans imanitè yo kòm santral pou adrese anpil defi sosyete imen an ap fè fas jodi a.

Epoutan, moun ki gen yon aktivite pwofesyonèl ki baze sou ansèyman lang ak kilti, an patikilye, ka gen rezon pou yo gen dout sou optimis sa a. Asosyasyon Lang Modèn te rapòte yon rediksyon de 29.3% nan enskripsyon lang ant 2009 ak 2021 (Lusin et al. 2023, 4), anvan lansman ChatGPT nan mwa novanm 2022 ak dènye ogmantasyon nan teknoloji ki gen rapò ak EA k ap alimante tradiksyon similtane. Nan yon atik Atlantic ki gen tit "Fen Edikasyon nan Lang Etranje", jounalis Louise Matsakis bay refleksyon apre li fin gade yon videyo tèt li "k ap pale Chinwa san fot" ke li te pwodwi lè l sèvi avèk EA (Matsakis 2024). Apple fòme itilizatè li yo "relye [b]baryè lang an pèsòn - pandan y ap vwayaje oswa navige nan yon peyi etranje - ak AirPods" (Apple 2025). Yon pèsepsyon k ap grandi ke etidye lang vin pa nesesè nan kontèks sa a, ansanm avèk aksan sou redwi depans ak efikasite k ap kondwi desizyon nan enstitisyon yo, sa ofri yon pèspektiv patetik pou pwogram lang atravè Etazini (Johnston 2025). Apre yo kanpe tout pwogram lang nan Inivèsite West Virginia an 2023, nouvèl sou konsolidasyon ak kloti pwogram lang yo, ki gen ladann enstitisyon rechèch an tèt yo, vin yon bagay ki komen.

Epitou, nou twouve nou nan yon tan kote anbrase lòt kilti ki alabaz plizyè rechèch syans imanitè yo atake. Nan dènye ane ki sot pase yo, yon bagay ou pa konn wè rankin ak laperèz, yo transfòme an entimidasyon ak difamasyon vyolan e deyimanizasyon moun ki diferan e souvan moun ki pi vilnerab nan mitan nou yo. Santiman anti-imigran ak rasis piblik nan peyi Etazini grandi nan yon nivo ke yo pa wè pandan plizyè deseni, yon reyalite ki vin pi entans depi janvye 2025 lan, jan dezyèm administrasyon Trump la fè aksyon anti-imigrasyon ak lejislasyon premye priyorite yo.

Popilasyon Amerik Latin ak Latino nan Etazini yo fè pati pami gwoup ki patikilyèman afekte pa ostilite piblik sa a. Ajan ICE yo maske, yo kidnape moun Latino nan kay ak kominote yo epi yo mete yo nan prizon san pwosedi regilye nan sant detansyon enprovize Ozetazini, tankou "Alligator Alcatraz" nan Florid, ak nan etablisman aletranje, tankou CECOT (Centro de Confinamiento del Terrorismo/Terrorism Confinement Center), yon gwo-prizon nan El Salvador (Fadel et al., 2025) (Morel and Gordon, 2025) (Graham, 2025). Administrasyon Trump la revoke Estati Pwoteksyon Tanporè (TPS) pou Ayisyen ak Venezyelyen k ap viv Ozetazini (Depatman Sekirite Enteryè, 2025a) (2025b). Anpil imigran ezite kite kay yo paske yo pè pou yo pa mete yo nan prizon, yon laperèz ki konfime pa dènye desizyon Lakou Siprèm nan ki apwouve mezi lapolis ki baze sou pwofil rasyal (Carcamo et al., 2025) (Jiménez et al., 2025) (Ryan et al., 2025).

Etidyan ki soti nan Amerik Latin yo ap fè fas ak defi non sèlman nan sosyete a, men tou nan kontèks patikilye edikasyon siperyè. Yo fè pati de kominote ki istorikman te rankontre baryè pou antre nan sistèm nan epi ki te lite pou fini ak diplòm yo, akoz de fado finansye ak responsablite familyal ke yo souvan dwe balanse ak etid yo (Genthe and Harrington, 2022) (Gonzalez, 2024) (Weissman, 2024). Demantèlman diskriminasyon pozitiv, elimine finansman pou inisyativ ak pwogram inivèsite ki vize pou ankouraje divèsite ak enklizyon, ak dènye sispansyon sibvansyon gouvènman federal la bay Enstitisyon k ap Sèvi Panyòl yo (Depatman Edikasyon Etazini, 2025) vin agrave sitiyasyon etidyan sa yo, ki souvan pa rekonèt tèt yo pami pwofesè yo ak etidyan parèy yo epi ki pa jwenn yon sans apatenans.

An menm tan an, lit gwoup majinalize yo nan Amerik Latin nan kontinye san rete. Nan anpil kote, vyolans kont fanm ak moun LGBTQIA+ vin tounen yon bagay ki nòmal nan lavi moun chak jou. Kominote endijèn yo ap fè fas ak diskriminasyon, destriksyon tè yo, ak efò pèsistan pou efase yo nan sosyete a. Moun ki desandan Afriken nan tout rejyon an dwe toujou goumen pou rekonesans jistis, ak patisipasyon egal ego nan sosyete yo ki depi lontan te minimize kontribisyon yo oswa nye egzistans yo. Lidè kominotè yo ak aktivis ki reziste kont enjistis ,yo pini yo regilyèman ak asasinen yo (da Silva Ribeiro Gomes, 2024) (Nieto-Matiz 2025).

Fas ak tout reyalite sa yo, bezwen pou nouvo apwòch sou rechèch nan syans imanitè yo vin pi ijan pase tout tan. Etidyan yo dwe ekspoze aktivite yo nan espas piblik epi angaje yo ak moun ki pa nan akademi an. Yo dwe demontre valè travay yo. Yo menm tou, yo dwe ofri etidyan yo opòtinite pou yo fè eksperyans fòmasyon andeyò sal klas la epi ede etidyan ki soti nan Amerik Latin yo jwenn fason pou kreye pwòp espas yo nan edikasyon siperyè ak pi lwen. Moun ki gen travay ki konsène moun ki majinalize yo dwe bati solidarite ak kominote sa yo epi ko-kreye pi bon pratik pou travay ansanm.

Pwojè yo prezante nan edisyon espesyal sa a, an patikilye, sèvi ak konesans kominote a kòm yon premye pa nan opozisyon oswa reziste kont fachis ak sipremasi blan, ni an dedan ak an deyò enstitisyon akademik yo. Pou nou retounen nan premye liy entwodiksyon sa a fòs pwojè sa yo pa chita nan zouti nimerik oswa metòd yo, men pito nan relasyon imen yo ki konstwi ak sipòte atravè disiplin yo ak pami entèvenan kominotè yo, ke vwa yo te istorikman majinalize, pafwa menm lè y ap rakonte pwòp istwa yo. Ann konsidere Ayiti, yon nasyon Nwa nan Amerik Latin nan ki, anplis ap pote chay imedya katastwòf klimatik ki te koze pa aksyon antrepriz yo ki nan Nò Global la, kontinye fè fas ak rasis ak vyolans tipik nan medya Amerik Nò ak entènasyonal. Jan Gina Athena Ulysse 1(2015)1, yon entèlektyèl-aktivis, fè nou sonje , Istwa Ayiti a merite yon"nouvo naratif"—ki pou Ayisyen e ekri pa Ayisyen. Atik ki nan edisyon espesyal sa yo mete aksan sou enpòtans relasyon imen ak responsablite kominotè nan kad pwojè ki pi laj yo pou batay kont lojik ejemonik, rasis, ak fachis ki kontinye defini kiyès ki imen nan laj nimerik la.

head.hi: Apwòch nan Amerik Latin nan ak Latino DH Ozetazini, ak Gwo Enplikasyon yo

div.p: Edisyon espesyal sa a prezante atik yo sou yon seri pwojè nimerik ki konsantre sou Amerik Latin nan ak popilasyon Latino ki pale de nosyon syans imanitè ki pi angaje e ki devwe sosyalman. Yo konsakre sou bati koneksyon avèk kominote yo, fè chanjman nan mond reyèl la, ak eksplore mòd kolaborasyon nan kreyasyon konesans. Yo tout bati sou fondasyon teyorik sofistike men yo fè travay yo nan espas ki aksesib kote piblik ki pa akademik yo envesti. Konsantre sou entèraksyon imen ki gen sans nan sant syans imanitè yo, chak pwojè yo sijere fason ke rechèch nou yo ak ansèyman nou yo ka kreye eksperyans an komen kote teknoloji pa ka ranplase moun reyèl. Yo demontre fason nou ka aprann entèvni nan fason sosyete a itilize teknoloji ak fòme li atravè yon apwòch imanis.

Chak pwojè genyen yon valè ki ale pi lwen pase pwòp valè patikilye li, li reprezante yon modèl pou yon kalite rechèch ke lòt moun ka imite oswa adapte. Lè yo aplike apwòch tankou istwa oral nimerik, itilizasyon rezo sosyo yo kòm zouti pou kominikasyon akademik ak kontribisyon kominotè, ak rekiperasyon e transmisyon materyèl eritaj kiltirèl, sa yo pwouve fason ke metodoloji espesifik yo ka deplwaye pou reyalize rechèch ki kolaboratif ak dinamik. Pwojè sa yo montre ke metòd inovatè pou entegre metòd nimerik nan sal klas premye sik yo, epi egzanp apwòch pou repanse wòl entèlektyèl ak pwofesè yo pi lwen pase lakou lekòl la nan espas piblik la.

Otè chak atik yo fè yo analiz kritik sou kijan travay yo gen rapò ak konsèp kominote, aktivis, ak inovasyon. Pa mwayen sa a, yo diskite sou eksperyans yo nan fè rechèch pou piblik la, yo eksplike modèl kolaborasyon yo te devlope, epi yo konsidere wòl travay sa a nan ansèyman ak angajman sivik yo. Yo analize aspè etik pwojè yo ak responsablite yo antanke entelektyèl, epi nan kèk ka antanke manm kominote espesifik yo, k ap travay pi lwen pase espas akademik tradisyonèl yo. Yo analize pwoblèm pozisyon, yo konsidere ki jan yo parèt tèt yo selon relasyon yo ak kominote y ap etidye yo oswa ak kiyès y ap kolabore.

Malgre edisyon sa a konsantre espesyalman sou pwoblèm pratik DH atravè etid Amerik Latin ak kominote Latino nan peyi Etazini, koleksyon an abòde pwoblèm jeneral nan syans imanitè nimerik yo globalman. Tout atik yo adrese misyon an, jan DHQ te eksprime li, pou "reyalize chanjman sosyal ak jistis sosyal, epi pou rann domèn syans imanitè nimerik la vizib tankou yon espas pou egalite rasyal ak sèks" ("Konsènan DHQ"). Yo reyalize sa lè yo bay entelektyèl ki pa blan yo yon platfòm pou diskite, sou pwòp kondisyon yo, de defi ki genyen fè travay akademik ki enpòtan pou kominote yo. Pifò nan kontribitè edisyon espesyal sa idantifye yo kòm moun ki pa blan epi yo travay nan tradisyon akademik ak kiltirèl ki pa reprezante ase nan rechèch DH ak espas enstitisyonèl yo.

Menm jan an tou, kòm majorite nan kontribitè nan edisyon espesyal yo se fanm, nou kwè pwojè sa a mete aksan sou lidèchip ke fanm entèlektyèl yo ap jwe nan devlopman travay transfòmasyon nan DH piblik. Non sèlman efò yo souvan konsantre sou eksperyans sèks ak entèseksyonalite, men yo demontre tou ke potansyèl metòd nimerik pou klarifye ak konbat lojik patriyaka ak sipremasi blan pandan y ap opere nan espas edikasyon siperyè ak rechèch. Travay yo konsantre sou bati kominote yo ak redefini objektif akademik nan kontèks ansèyman, rechèch ak sèvis, epi divès apwòch akademik yo sijere fason pou defye paradigm patriyakal ak rasis yo lè yo mete aksan sou metodoloji ki mete aksan sou enpati, konsyans pwòp tèt ou, respè pou diferans, estrikti ki pa yerachize, pratik etik ak atansyon sou entèseksyonalite.

Edisyon espesyal sa a selebre yon lòt kalite divèsite, li mete aksan sou vwa jèn entelektyèl yo. Twa nan kat editè envite yo ak pifò nan otè yo se entelektyèl ki nan kòmansman karyè yo. Nan fason sa a, koleksyon an montre angajman kominote DH la pou kreye espas pou lide jèn entelektyèl yo ki, malgre sikonstans pwofesyonèl difisil ke yo souvan fè fas nan akademi jodi a, y ap travay kreyativman san pran souf pou defini avni domèn nan.

Nou kwè ke edisyon espesyal sa a kontribye nan pwomosyon entènasyonal, karaktè miltileng nan syans imanitè nimerik yo. Koleksyon sa a mete aksan sou yon jewografi DH la ki devlope pi lwen pase limit mond anglofòn nan ak Ewòp oksidantal la, li rive nan espas kiltirèl atravè Amerik Latin ak Karayib la epi li eksplore jewografi transnasyonal, transfwontyè, ak dyasporik yo ki souvan envizib nan kominote Etazini ki gen rasin yo nan rejyon sa yo. Editè ak otè yo vle abòde kesyon sou kisa sa vle di fè DH nan lòt lang ki pa anglè, epi, apre premye piblikasyon edisyon espesyal sa a, yo pral pibliye chak atik nan omwen yon lòt lang: Panyòl, Fransè, oswa Kreyòl Ayisyen. Y ap pibliye yon adisyon nan entwodiksyon sa a yon fwa yo entegre tout tradiksyon yo.

Edisyon espesyal sa a kesyone tou sou fason nou defini DH, kòm repons a apèl regilye DHQ a pou kontribisyon ki “eksplore limit domèn lan oswa re-egzamine fondasyon li yo.” Atik ki nan koleksyon espesyal sa a demontre yon kalite DH ki pa privilejye ni imanite dijital yo ni syans imanitè tradisyonèl yo, men pito sèvi ak zouti dijital ak kad imanite yo pou angaje yo ak kominote reyèl yo ak defi yo fè fas a. DH li menm konsidere tèt li kòm yon tip de "syans imanitè aplike," men pwojè sa yo ale pi lwen, objektif yo se travay nan sèvis ki fè yon diferans reyèl ak imedya pou moun ke sosyete a ak akademi a neglije. Kidonk, edisyon espesyal sa a ap chèche pale ak yon DH aktif, angaje ki alafwa politik ak totalman pèsonèl.

Lè n abòde tèm sa yo, koleksyon sa a swiv tras plizyè edisyon espesyal DHQ te pibliye dènyeman. Atravè konsantrasyon li sou divèsite ak enklizyon, edisyon sa a konekte avèk Black Digital Humanities in the Rising Generation (Syans Imanitè Nimerik Nwa nan Jenerasyon k ap vini) (16.3, 2022), Minimal Computing (16.2, 2022), Digital Sankofa: Understanding the Past and Futures of Black Digital Humanities (Konprann Pase ak Avni Syans Imanitè Nwa yo) (18.4, 2024), ak pi resan, The Politics and Ethics of Naming the Name of Slave People in Digital Humanities Projects ( Politik ak Etik Pou Nonmen Non Moun Esklav nan Pwojè Syans Imanitè Nimerik yo) (19.1, 2025). Lè w mete aksan sou tradisyon ki pa anglofòn, edisyon sa a gen rapò tou ak edisyon espesyal sou DH an Panyòl (12.1, 2018) ak Pòtigè (14.2, 2020), ansanm ak koleksyon Digital Humanities & Colonial Latin American Studies ( Syans Imanitè Nimerik at Etid Kolonyal Amerik Latin nan) (14.4, 2020). Lè otè yo konsantre sou enplikasyon pedagojik travay yo , yo abòde sijè ki gen rapò ak Imagining the DH Undergraduate: Special Issue in Undergraduate Education in DH (11.3, 2017).

Sylvia Fernández Quintanilla, Maira E. Álvarez, Carolina E. Alonso, ak Laura Gonzales analize United Fronteras, yon kolektif aktivis ak entelektyèl ki etidye fwontyè Meksik ak Etazini kòm yon espas varye ki chaje ak plizyè kouch siyifikasyon ki reprezante piblikman ak nimerikman atravè diferan fòm ak media. Gwoup sa, ki gen ladan plis fanm ki pa blan te fè eksperyans rejyon fwontyè a nan diferan fason, ko-kreye yon depo resous materyèl nimerik ak pwojè ki abòde pwoblèm enpòtan nan kominote yo sou tou de bò fwontyè a ki enkonsistan e ki imajinè, sa soti depi anvan epòk kolonyal la rive jouk jodi a. Nan atik yo a, yo konsidere fason pwojè a itilize enfòmatik minimal nan pwojè a ak angajman li nan zafè istwa kiltirèl, vyolans politik ak sèks, yon fason pou revele konpleksite nan espas imen ki souvan dekri sou yon tèm senp e negatif.

Siobhan Meï ak Jonathan Michael Square reflechi sou eksperyans yo kòm ko-fondatè ak direktè Rendering Revolution: Apwòch Satoryal de Istwa Ayisyen. Pwojè a defini tèt li kòm "yon eksperyans omoseksyèl, bileng, feminis nan rechèch entèdisiplinè nimerik ki itilize lantiy mòd ak kilti materyèl yo pou trase estetik, sosyal, ak konsekans politik nan Revolisyon Ayisyen an kòm yon moman istorik mondyal." Meï ak Square egzamine efò kolaborasyon yon ekip ki gen ekspètiz li nan tradiksyon, kilti vizyèl, ak teyori kiltirèl, ak itilizasyon pwojè a sou Instagram kòm yon platfòm pou analize istwa ak kilti Ayisyen. Prezante tankou yon konvèsasyon ant de otè yo, kontribisyon yo montre kijan Rendering Revolution konekte tan pase ak prezan yon fason ki vizyèlman frapan epi li defann pouvwa rezo sosyo kòm yon zouti pou kominikasyon akademik.

Constanza López Baquero analize Voces y Caras: Latinx Communities of North Florida (Kominote Latino nan Nò Florid), yon pwojè istwa oral kote etidyan Latino yo konsevwa ak fè entèvyou lokal ak rezidan Panyòl yo nan Inivèsite North Florida Pandan trèz dènye ane yo, yon santèn etidyan ak manm kominote yo te patisipe, yo bati yon gwo achiv istwa ki konsantre sou reyalite imigrasyon yo, eksperyans fanm yo nan kilti Ispanik yo, ak divèsite yo te jwenn nan mitan moun ki gen orijin yo nan Amerik Latin nan, ki Ozetazini. Nan atik la, López Baquero rakonte istwa pwojè a, li mete aksan sou yon seleksyon entèvyou, epi eksplike kijan, pwojè a— atravè eleman nimerik ak ki pa nimerik — li montre pèspektiv kominote yo ki otreman rete lajman envizib nan rejyon an.

Nicole Willson konsidere Fanm Rebèl: Fouye Istwa Fanm Ayisyèn Revolisyonè yo, yon pwojè rechèch de twa lane ki patwone pa Leverhulme Trust ak Enstiti pou Rechèch Atlantik Nwa nan Inivèsite Central Lancashire. Fanm Rebèl ap chèche fouye istwa fanm nan Revolisyon Ayisyen an, mete aksan sou zak radikal rebelyon ak maronaj fi yo epi eksplore istwa rezistans ki defini nan pratik espirityèl, travay domestik, kreyativite, siviv, desepsyon ak lit ame. Nan atik li a, Willson wè pwojè a kòm yon espas pou kolaborasyon ant entelektyèl, kolesyonè, konsèvatè, achivis ak lòt pati ki enterese de kominote a.

Elvira Aballí Morell eksplike kijan depo kolaborasyon atizay nimerik ContArte Latinoamérica ap chèche ankouraje ak montre pwodiksyon atistik kominote Latino Ozetazini yo nan kreyasyon opòtinite pedagojik ak atravè sensibilizasyon piblik. Pwojè sa enplike etidyan yo kòm kolaboratè nan bati achiv la ak fè atelye kominotè ki vize a popilasyon Latinxo nan Nashville, kote ContArte chita. Aballí Morell analize kijan pwojè a ede etidyan yo vin sitwayen aktif, li mete aksan sou enpòtans patisipasyon ak kontribisyon yo nan inivèsite ak nan kominote ki ozatantou yo.

Lauren Royes-Baccus reflechi sou Salt & Aloes tankou yon platfòm nimerik pou sistèm radikal pataj konesans kote materyèl Karayib la ak kilti vizyèl ka reimajine, reoryante, ak resevwa resous. Pwojè a ap chèche derasinen rejyon an de yon konsepsyon estetik ak yon pwojeksyon ki baze sou yon lòt abstrè ak pasif. Royes-Baccus egzaminen kijan travay Salt & Aloes mete aksan sou itilizasyon aktif ak transfòmasyon objè Karayib la, pratik jeneratif kreyatif ki soti de/andedan/nan rejyon an, ak restitisyon materyèl pase li, prezan ak avni li yo.

Sylvia Mendoza Aviña konsidere MAS Muxeres: Istwa oral nan Chicana/x lidè nan Pwogram Etid Meksiken Ameriken nan San Antonio, Texas, tankou yon istwa oral ak pwojè syans imanitè nimerik ki dokimante kontribisyon fanm k ap travay pou kenbe domèn nan vivan epi pwospere. Malgre efò yo fè chak jou pou sipòte etid MAS/Chicanx nan wòl yo kòm kowòdonatè pwogram, enstriktè/pwofesè, òganizatè kominotè, ak aktivis akademik, anpil nan memwa enstitisyonèl, òganizasyon, ak estrateji muxeres sa yo rete san yo pa dokimante. Mendoza Aviña deklare ke konesans yo itil e yo nesesè pou jenerasyon aktyèl la ak jenerasyon k ap vini yo espesyalman moun ki vle envesti nan soutni, e konstwi etid MAS/Chicana yo, espesyalman nan kote tankou Texas k ap eseye plis blanchi kourikoulòm ak tèks yo atravè pwopozisyon la lwa ki atake teyori ras kritik, divèsite, ekite ak enklizyon (DEI), ak libète akademik.

Robert Irwin eksplore Humanizing Deportation (Imanize Depòtasyon), yon pwojè odyovizyèl patisipatif ki depi kòmansman ane 2017 l ap dokimante epi simaye konsekans migrasyon kontanporen ak lwa ak politik kontwòl fwontyè (genyen) sou imigran vilnerab Ozetazini ak Meksik. Atravè kolaborasyon sou teren an avèk imigran depòte ak moun k ap chèche azil nan Tijuana ak lòt kote, pwojè a te pibliye plis pase 450 istwa nimerik sou sit entènèt bileng li a. Irwin konsidere kijan Humanizing Deportation te devlope plis estrateji pou entegre elèv sik klasik yo nan ekip rechèch li a, sa pèmèt elèv sa yo ke anpil nan yo gen fanmi yo ki afekte pa lwa ak politik sa yo, vin patisipe dirèkteman epi se yon fason ki enpòtan nan ede imigran yo kominike eksperyans ak enkyetid yo bay mond la.

Eduard Arriaga-Arango etidye Baobaixa, yon inisyativ rezo Afro-Brezilyen Rede Mocambos devlope ki sèvi kòm yon modèl òganizasyon kominotè nimerik kòm yon fason pou ankouraje jistis done, souverènte nimerik ak otonomi. Baobaixa se yon teknoloji ki konekte divès kominote nan Brezil (tankou, Quilombos, kominote Endijèn ak Favelas, pami lòt), epi tou li kreye yon estrikti pou estoke, seleksyone ak simaye konesans lokal, tradisyon yo, istwa ak reprezantasyon yo. Nan atik li a, Arriaga-Arango pwopoze Baobaixa kòm yon modèl pou kijan kominote ki pa ekspè yo ka itilize estrateji nimerik pou defann teritwa yo, prezève pwodiksyon kiltirèl yo, ak afime kondisyon imanite yo.

Edisyon espesyal sa a montre yon seri de efò sa yo, ki reflete nan pwojè nimerik yo (ki an pwosesis oswa ki fini) kote teknoloji enpòtan men pa poukont li, men pito pou fason li pèmèt entèlektyèl yo fè aktivite ki esansyèl men ki pa nimerik nan nati. Lè nou deklare ke itilize teknoloji kapab itil— men se pa sa ki enpòtan — nou kwè atik ki la yo kontribye nan mete aksan sou yon paradoks nan pèsepsyon moun ki pa nan domèn DH la genyen depi lontan. Referans "STEM pou syans imanitè yo" atire administratè yo epi li pwovoke sispisyon nan mitan chèchè akademik tradisyonèl yo, li mete aksan sou entegrasyon zouti nimerik an rechèch syans imanitè kòmsi li fè pati de teknoloji. Atik ki la yo montre ke, fason anpil travay nan syans imanitè nimerik yo jodi a pa konsantre fondamantalman sou teknoloji, men pito sou sijè yo ki, nan kèk kontèks politik ak enstitisyonèl, ka rann moun k ap pran desizyon yo malalèz epi kòlèg nou yo andeyò DH ta ka rekonèt kòm reprezantatè kontinwite travay la nan syans imanitè tradisyonèl yo.

Yon gwo pati nan DH rete konsantre anpil sou enfòmatik nan nati li epi anpil travay soti nan kesyon yo ki plis anrasinnen nan syans enfòmatik olye de syans imanitè tradisyonèl yo. Sepandan, nan dènye ane yo ekspansyon domèn nan te pote yon pi gwo rekonesans ke DH souvan enplike itilizazyon zouti nimerik pou konbat enjistis ak konstwi kominote yo, efè travay sa yo montre nouvo fason ke syans imanitè yo ka angaje yo ak piblik la epi montre enpòtans yo nan yon mond kote eksperyans imen an ap devalorize de jou an jou. Menm jan ak plizyè nan pwojè yo ke nou mete aksan sou yo isit la, efò sa yo souvan enplike etidyan yo epi souvan sa mande yon refleksyon sou kolaborasyon nou yo ansanm ak yon reevalyasyon sou sa nou anseye, kijan, ak poukisa.

Lè yo reyini konsèp kominotè ak aktivis — toulède santral nan rechèch Amerik Latin ak Latino—avèk yon gwo atansyon sou nosyon entèvansyon, inovasyon, ak envansyon ki karakterize DH, koleksyon miltileng sa a fè referans sou fason ke kominote imanis ak imanis nimerik yo ka aprann de travay k ap fèt avèk divès popilasyon ki te siviv enjistis istorik epi ki kontinye ap soufri e reziste majinalizasyon jodi a, tou de nan peyi Etazini ak atravè tout Amerik Latin ak Karayib la. Espeyalman, n ap mete aksan sou travay entelektyèl entèdisiplinè ki pa blan, fanm entelektyèl, ak chèchè ki nan kòmansman karyè yo , edisyon espesyal sa a ofri modèl yo pou konsepsyon pratik, angage syans imanitè pa egzanp ki ka pi byen satisfè bezwen etidyan miltileng ak miltikiltirèl ak divès kominote pi lwen pase akademi an ak franchi limit jewografi yo.
